answer: At most 4 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a tundra tag. The lagoon cap is checked at intake and velvet makes public the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool therefore cannot mint a army of identities in one epoch regardless of capital it holds, because each identity consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. That is 16 dollars per alias. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
